changes.current_line: Customers see an average uplift in authorization rates with Authorization Boost and Adaptive Acceptance.
changes.change: For payments leaders who ask for their own numbers, lead with: Your approvals, market by market: by country, card type and issuer, with the reason for each decline pattern and the money left on the table. Use 'approvals' in the headline and keep 'authorization', Authorization Boost and Adaptive Acceptance for the technical detail underneath. Do not lead with the average uplift.
changes.why: Stefan rejected the average outright ('that's an average. What's mine?'), defined proof as country, card type, issuer and why, and speaks of approvals and money left on the table rather than authorization and uplift.

changes.change: When a buyer is weighing a 'local acquiring' test, offer a per-country approvals diagnostic on their own traffic, with a committed delivery date that lands before the competitor's test ends. Suggested line: Before you decide, see your own approvals by country, card type and issuer, and why, from your own traffic. Confirm a realistic turnaround with the payments performance team before promising it, and only mention local routing where product confirms we offer it.
changes.why: Adyen won by testing his own traffic and reporting results by country, and our market-by-market analysis was the most useful thing we sent him but arrived three weeks after he asked, once the test had finished.

changes.current_line: Support plans with tiered response times, up to 24/7 coverage.
changes.change: For payments owners, lead with a named person at Stripe who reviews your approvals every month, instead of response-time tiers. Suggested line: A named payments performance owner who looks at your numbers every month. Confirm with account management that we can staff this before using it.
changes.why: Stefan asked who at Stripe looks at his numbers every month and the rep had no name, he turned down the roadmap session, and he read our outreach as reactive ('I heard from Stripe when I said I was leaving.').

changes.change: Add a proof point the champion can take to the CFO: this customer's own approvals and the revenue at stake per market, set out in a short readout rather than a benchmark. Suggested framing: Here is the money left on the table in each of your markets, and what we would fix.
changes.why: The CFO approved Stefan's recommendation, and Stefan said plainly 'I can't take an average to my CFO.', so our proof had to work in a room we were never in.
